claims.text: How Does the USA Compare on Health Spending?
claims.support: USA current health expenditure is 16.69414902% of GDP (rank 1)
Indicator measures current health expenditure as a percentage of GDP

claims.text: Comparing current health expenditure as a percentage of GDP across nations using World Bank data.
claims.support: Level of current health expenditure expressed as a percentage of GDP, source World Bank (Global Health Expenditure Database)

claims.text: The United States spends 16.7% of its economy on health. Bangladesh spends just 2.2%.
That puts the American system at the very top of global spending.
claims.support: USA rank 1 out of 189 mapped entities

claims.text: The United States spends 5.1 times as much as India, where health receives 3.3%.
claims.support: USA value 16.69414902 / IND value 3.33944035 = 4.999 (approx 5 times), IND display 3.3%

claims.text: Major European economies spend heavy too: Germany sits at 12.3%, Austria at 11.8%, France at 11.5%, and the UK at 11.1%.
Yet in Nigeria, current health spending accounts for 4.2% of GDP.
This counts medical goods and services consumed, excluding capital costs like hospitals or emergency vaccine stocks.
claims.support: Estimates of current health expenditures include healthcare goods and services consumed during each year. This indicator does not include capital health expenditures such as buildings, machinery, IT and stocks of vaccines for emergency or outbreaks.
